image.title: DW
image.description: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

item.title: ICC unseals Taliban leaders' warrants over persecuting women
item.description: The court gave more details on the warrants for four Taliban leaders accused of the crime against humanity of gender persecution of women, girls and the LGBTQ+ community. The Islamist group rejected the warrants.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Australia's migrant policy offers lessons for EU and US
item.description: Australia has used offshore processing centers to deter asylum seekers for more than two decades. As the EU and US pursue similar third-country arrangements, Australia's experience highlights the potential problems.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Yemen launches major military operation against Houthis
item.description: Yemen's internationally recognized government has launched a new military offensive to retake Houthi-held territory, as the Iran-backed rebel group claims new attacks in Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Denmark: Data of millions compromised in hack
item.description: The breach by the hackers was through the legitimate login credentials of a local company, initial findings suggest. The data of some 8.8 million registered people was compromised.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
item.description: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Ukraine says Russian drones behind Turkish ship sinking
item.description: Romanian authorities did not say what caused the fire, but local media reported that the ship was carrying grain and was hit by a drone.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Australia, New Zealand probe Flydubai pilot's time there
item.description: The Flydubai pilot from Oman suspected of trying to crash a plane in Israel spent time in Oceania as a young man. Police in both Australia and New Zealand said they would investigate his links to the countries.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Euro plummets against US dollar: has the next financial crisis begun?
item.description: The euro has fallen to a 17-month low against the dollar. That will make inflation worse in the EU, where political worries and concern over French debt are already troubling investors. Is a fiscal crisis at hand?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Military aircraft with 32 people on board crashes in southern Nigeria
item.description: Rescue teams searched the crash site after the military aircraft went down in southern Nigeria. All 32 people on the plane are confirmed to have died.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Iran poised to exploit security vacuum as US leaves Iraq
item.description: The end of the US military mission in Iraq leaves the Kurdistan region facing a severe security vacuum. As Erbil grapples with deep internal divisions, Tehran is well positioned to make strategic gains.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Trust in the German Constitutional Court is eroding — how can this be stopped?
item.description: Germany's top court, which turned 75 this year, is losing the population's trust, surveys show. Some say reforms in the way it picks candidates would help, to also accept candidates nominated by the far-right AfD.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: What China's new military foothold in Laos means for Southeast Asia
item.description: Beijing says its new Laos facility will train pilots. Analysts see a broader signal: China's growing military presence in mainland Southeast Asia.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany news: Spy chief warns Russia conflict risk growing
item.description: Moscow is already waging a "shadow war" against Europe, the head of Germany's foreign intelligence service says. The Left Party is taking a case over remarks by the CDU's Katherina Reiche to a top court. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
item.description: A worker at a plague research institute in Siberia has died, and nearly 200 of her contacts are under medical observation. Russian authorities deny a link to the bacterial infection. The US is monitoring the situation.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: German soccer: Can new coach Klopp turn things around?
item.description: Jürgen Klopp has done things a little differently since becoming Germany coach. Casting a wider net for talent and trying to connect with players and country haven't made an immediate impact, but he is not bowed.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Bosnia election: New steps to prevent electoral fraud, but nationalist parties remain on top
item.description: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: German and US scientists win Nobel Prize in medicine for research on brain activity
item.description: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the award for discoveries that provide new insights into how we might treat blindness, depression, addiction and dementia.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: As rising seas threaten low-lying Pacific Islands, regional leaders call on the world to take climate more seriously
item.description: For Pacific island nations, climate change is no distant threat. As seas rise, they're bringing the real-time consequences of a warming planet directly to world leaders in Tuvalu.
item.dc:subject: Climate

item.title: Israel's mental health crisis in the wake of Oct. 7 attacks
item.description: More than a third of Israelis have shown symptoms of mental health conditions, a report found. Three years after the October 7 attack, the country's health system is still struggling to come to terms with its effects.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Israel observes October 7 anniversary with national memorial day
item.description: Israel is holding memorial ceremonies nationwide for those killed in the October 7, 2023 Hamas terror attacks and soldiers who died in the ensuing war.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Hundreds of French schools shut, teen loses hand in protests
item.description: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. A teenage boy lost his hand, seemingly while trying to pick up a police tear gas grenade.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
item.description: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: UK remands 2 Iranians over alleged antisemitic terror plot
item.description: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur and later charged with plotting to attack Jewish targets in Manchester.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions
item.description: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: German reunification: How inequality is shaping a new East German identity
item.description: A new study highlights persistent structural disparities in wealth and leadership positions between East and West Germany, 36 years after reunification.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Spain's parliament rejects housing bill as protests continue
item.description: Spain's minority government suffered defeat in parliament as it tried to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. A pensioner's eviction and protests led to the bid.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: "NAZA": Israeli military issues statement on film
item.description: The award-winning documentary "NAZA" continues to spark controversy in Israel. The Israeli military has now published a multi-page statement calling the film's portrayal "distorted."
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany's Franz Reindl elected new IIHF president
item.description: Franz Reindl has been elected president of ice hockey's world governing body. The former forward was a member of West Germany's Olympic bronze medal-winning team.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Climate leaders called for solar energy for 'everyone, everywhere' by 2030, but with three years to go, is that goal attainable?
item.description: Prominent climate leaders have called on governments, businesses, institutions and the public to make a push for solar power before the decade is out, repowering the world with cheap, clean energy. Is that possible?
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Manchester City Premier League charges: What do they mean?
item.description: Since being bought by the UAE in 2008, Manchester City have become one of the world's most successful football clubs. A raft of serious financial charges threatens to undermine this and bring chaos to the Premier League.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: ARD-Deutschlandtrend survey: Germans unite in frustration over the government
item.description: On the 36th anniversary of reunification, Germans are dissatisfied with the country's political leaders. They don't believe they'll be able to handle the challenges posed by AI, Russia and Donald Trump.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
item.description: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
item.description: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: EU ministers mull new ways to curb irregular migration
item.description: The proposals include setting up so-called return hubs outside the EU and strengthening the border agency Frontex. Greece has even proposed temporarily suspending asylum applications in emergency situations.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Klopp wins first game as Germany coach, without 'top dogs'
item.description: It may have taken a little longer than he would have liked, but Jürgen Klopp has finally won a game as Germany coach. Despite a number of debutants, it was a familiar face who stood out in the victory over Serbia.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Latvians head to the polls with Russia on their minds
item.description: On October 3, Latvians will elect a new parliament with Russia looming large over the campaign. Security fears dominate the agenda, but so does a debate over the economic cost of cutting ties with Moscow.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could see drivers pay higher running costs while also increasing carbon emissions.
item.description: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could yet see drivers pay higher running costs while increasing planet-heating emissions.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Germans' biggest fear is the high cost of living, an annual study finds
item.description: What do Germans fear most in 2026? Wars? Global crises? Wrong. Their biggest concern is the cost of living, which keeps rising.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Germany news: Merz lauds NATO with Westphalian Peace Prize
item.description: At a ceremony to honor NATO, the German chancellor warned that Russia will threaten the rest of Europe if it isn't stopped in Ukraine. In other news, the German military will set up its first drone regiment.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
item.description: Student protests have grown in scale and intensity, with violent clashes in some places leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
item.description: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers for rejected asylum seekers outside the EU.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany debates alleged antisemitism in the Left Party
item.description: The Central Council of Jews in Germany thinks the Left Party is dangerous. Other Jews, however, are showing solidarity with the party. How does that add up?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
item.description: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
item.description: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
item.description: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?
item.description: Donald Trump thinks the name artificial intelligence sounds "fake" and has ordered US agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead. Yet, tech firms and researchers have little reason to play along.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
item.description: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany news: Volkswagen ends collective wage agreements
item.description: In an effort to cut costs, automaker Volkswagen terminated most of its collective wage agreements in Germany. This could reignite disputes with employee representatives.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: El Nino is a 'postcard from the future' — and could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths
item.description: The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picks up speed
item.description: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar vowed to dismantle Orban's corrupt networks. High-profile figures are being arrested and many Hungarians are pushing for swift accountability, but the rule of law takes time.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: South Park satirist pushes for accountability in Cornell gang-rape lawsuit
item.description: Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
item.description: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Albania: As corruption cases multiply, experts question whether the anti-corruption drive is addressing the causes or just the symptoms.
item.description: From a former president to the ex-intelligence chief, Albania is prosecuting senior officials at a rate once thought impossible. But do more prosecutions mean less corruption or simply better enforcement?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Global trade weathers Iran, Ukraine and Trump's tariffs
item.description: Over the past six years, COVID, two wars and Donald Trump's tariffs have shaken world trade. With globalization already stalling, is this a temporary shock or the start of a great reversal?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: AI: Concern as Germany plans to double data center capacity
item.description: Germany is rewriting the rules to attract data center investment from AI companies. But local communities are becoming increasingly skeptical.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Spain grows fruit and vegetables for Europe, but it's running out of water
item.description: Spain's southern coast produces up to 25% of Europe's fruit and vegetables. But amid intensive farming, climate change and illegal wells, the water it takes to grow them is drying up.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: UK: US government questions bail for Fairford base suspects
item.description: The US government sees "the hand of a foreign actor" in the security scare at RAF Fairford, a hub for US heavy bombers in Europe. Donald Trump criticized the suspects being released on bail amid ongoing investigations.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Sicily: Mount Etna ash disrupts Catania flights again
item.description: A thick ash cloud from Mount Etna has been disrupting flights to Catania in Sicily for several days. Italy and Europe's most active volcano, Etna has impacted air travel several times this summer.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Turkey: Comedian convicted for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
item.description: Deniz Goktas was convicted of two of three charges, including "insulting" the president, but was released pending the appeal process. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: What do Manchester City's charges mean for German football?
item.description: Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty of major financial rule breaches. What does this mean for German football?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany news: COVID vaccine maker BioNTech to close 3 sites
item.description: COVID-19 vaccine maker BioNTech is to close three sites in Germany after efforts to find buyers failed. Meanwhile, Rhine water levels have fallen to record lows after an unusually dry September. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Diesel prices are surging putting further pressure on Europe
item.description: Trucks, farms and industry are powered with diesel. Now prices are soaring due to refinery disruptions, supply shortages and geopolitical tensions. A potential US export ban could make Europe's diesel crunch even worse.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?
item.description: After defeat to Greece, Jürgen Klopp faces the first real test of his tenure as coach of Germany's national men's football team. Can his charisma alone push this group forward?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
item.description: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
item.description: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany news: Are Germans giving up their beloved meat and sausages?
item.description: Germans used to be all about sausages and meat. While those do remain popular, things seem to be slowly changing. There also are new insights into the economic side of East Germany's espionage DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
item.description: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: DW shows solidarity with Georgians' commitment to democracy
item.description: Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Bundesliga, other top European leagues call for major FIFA reforms
item.description: The Bundesliga and three other leading European football leagues have said major reforms to world-governing body FIFA are "essential." However, they stopped short of calling for the resignation of boss Gianni Infantino.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
item.description: A late Netherlands goal denied Jürgen Klopp a win in his first match as Germany coach. The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund boss has big ambitions, but the game showed he's going to need more time to achieve them.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Three-way battle for power in world chess: Who will be elected FIDE president in Samarkand?
item.description: The era of Russian presidents is coming to an end at the World Chess Federation (FIDE). Two Germans and one Kazakh are up for election. Among the issues at play are money, Kremlin influence, and unanswered questions.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: After several difficult years, economists now expect German economy to grow
item.description: Germany's economy is growing again, but recovery remains on shaky ground. High government spending is keeping the economy afloat, while energy prices, a shortage of skilled workers and debt continue to weigh on it.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Political psychology: Why extremist parties are thriving and what democratic politicians can do against it
item.description: Far-right and far-left parties are celebrating success after success, leaving moderate politicians in the dust and worrying many Germans. Political psychology helps us understand what's behind growing polarization.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
item.description: A study shows chatbots mirror users' politics, part of a broader tendency known as AI sycophancy. Researchers fear this could deepen polarization.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Germany news: Berlin officially withdraws Olympics bid
item.description: Berlin's decision to withdraw its Olympic bid means that only Munich and the western Rhine/Ruhr region are left in the running as potential Olympic hosts. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Could a Left Party government in Berlin expropriate large real estate companies?
item.description: The socialist Left Party won the Berlin election partly on the promise to implement the city's 2021 expropriation referendum as a way to solve the city's rent crisis. But can it really happen?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes
item.description: Three gold medals and three Asian Games records have catapulted China's Yu Zidi, 13, into the sporting spotlight. She is far from the first teen prodigy, but should teens be competing at elite level?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Germany's oldest party, the center-left SPD, is in a difficult position following its success in the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state election
item.description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) has vowed to press ahead with controversial reforms, but resistance is mounting within his coalition partner, the SPD. How much dissent can a governing coalition tolerate?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Munich and Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr – Germany's two remaining Olympic candidates
item.description: Munich or the Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr region? Germany aims to host the Olympic Games again. Just two candidates are left after Berlin pulled out at the last minute.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: El Nino explained: How the weather pattern affects hurricanes and tropical storms
item.description: From drought to major floods and extreme heat, El Nino will have a huge impact on the world's weather. In the Atlantic, it could mean a season without hurricanes.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: China's new travel rules unsettle tech giants and talent
item.description: Beijing is locking the gates to stop expertise and capital in strategic industries from fleeing. The country accused of industrial-scale intellectual property theft now fears the West will take its own.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany news: Call to scrap once-a-day gas price rises
item.description: The ADAC motoring association says a once-a-day rule on gas price changes has failed to help drivers' wallets. Entry-level jobs are becoming scarcer, making things hard for those entering the job market. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Young Berliners vote overwhelmingly for socialist Left Party
item.description: Berlin's young voters overwhelmingly supported the victorious socialist Left Party. Are the young more radical? Or are the election results just a reflection of current German politics?
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
item.description: Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.
item.dc:subject: Climate

item.title: Could we see MMA at the Olympics?
item.description: Mixed martial arts has made its debut at the Asian Games this week. It takes the sport closer to the Olympics, but there are doubts about the next step — and the influence of the popular and lucrative UFC.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
item.description: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
item.description: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany news: VW to step up cost-cutting program
item.description: Volkswagen's chief says the carmaker will accelerate its streamlining measures as workers protest. The Israeli ambassador says the Left Party win in Berlin polls poses a risk to the city's Jewish community. DW has more.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: How will Germany's Merz respond after crushing state election results and losses to the far right?
item.description: Germany's far-right AfD and the socialist Left Party gained ground in recent state elections, while the centrist parties lost support. The biggest loser is Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: Princess Diana's brother makes explosive claims about royals in new memoir
item.description: Here are some of the key revelations from Charles Earl Spencer's highly anticipated memoir "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." It has already provoked Buckingham Palace to react.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Germany news: Trial starts of ex-Transport Minister Scheuer
item.description: Former Transport Minister Andreas Scheuer is being tried for perjury related to a failed car toll scheme. And cherry farmers have brought in a bumper harvest.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Germany's car crisis: Can the 35-hour workweek survive?
item.description: German carmakers want employees to work 40 hours instead of the current 35 without extra pay, arguing it would improve competitiveness. Unions strongly oppose the proposal and view it as an attack on workers' rights.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
item.description: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue for the government. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Summer of 2026 broke records in Europe, and caused deaths
item.description: The summer of 2026 was not only the hottest on record in Europe, it also saw a record number of people die. More than 16,000 are thought to have died because of the heat in Germany alone.
item.dc:subject: Science

item.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know
item.description: This year, AI will be used to manage overcrowded situations. Find all the numbers surrounding the fest — including the price of water!
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Rebels, workers, radicals: The making of 'Red Berlin'
item.description: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

item.title: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
item.description: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz attacks spill oil into Persian Gulf
item.description: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.
item.dc:subject: Environment

item.title: Dual citizenship means Germany now in competition for talent
item.description: Coach Jürgen Klopp has named several players to his first Germany squad who are eligible to play for other countries. Some still aren't committed to playing for thje national team long-term.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Beethoven and Andy Warhol: Rebel icons on show in Bonn
item.description: The new exhibition "Beethoven by Warhol" at the Beethoven House in Bonn presents the pop artist's late masterpiece: a picture of Ludwig van Beethoven. The exhibition shares the story of the work with the public.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: VAR's mission creep a problem for football
item.description: After a decade of use, questions around VAR in football are louder than ever. Has the technology strayed too far from its remit?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
item.description: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Klopp wants Germany's football team to 'reclaim the flag'
item.description: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
item.description: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: Jürgen Klopp's first Germany squad includes 44 players
item.description: Germany's new head coach Jürgen Klopp has named a huge squad for his first four games, splitting them into two groups. A host of new faces is included.
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
item.description: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
item.description: A glacier and rock collapse in Nepal killed nearly 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Scientists say decades of warming helped set the disaster in motion.

item.title: After Neuer: Who will be Germany's new No. 1 goalkeeper?
item.description: Following Manuel Neuer's retirement, there are many candidates to succeed him, but which goalkeeper will Jürgen Klopp choose? What factors will play a role? And will Neuer's future have an indirect influence?
item.dc:subject: Sports

item.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'
item.description: Two decades of progress toward gender parity is at risk as women's political representation declines, according to a new World Economic Forum report. At the current pace, the remaining gap could take 120 years to close.

item.title: German drama 'Blindspot Berlin' revisits 2016 Christmas market attack
item.description: A decade after the terrorist attack on a Berlin Christmas market, a new German miniseries looks into the institutional failures that allowed the deadly truck rampage to happen.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: How extreme heat is hitting wallets
item.description: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

item.title: Spanish scientists find first evidence of Diplodocus dinosaur in Europe
item.description: Paleontologists in Spain say they have found the first evidence of the long-necked Diplodocus genus of dinosaur outside of North America. They found bones at the rich La Tejeria fossil site in Teruel in eastern Spain.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over
item.description: US debt has topped $40 trillion. How risky is the country's growing debt burden. And will investors keep funding Washington's deficits?
item.dc:subject: Business
